Lessons.Title: Representations of Equal Groups of Fractions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will interpret and generate diagrams and expressions that represent multiplication of a whole number and a unit fraction in order to find the value of the product.
Key idea: Equivalent unit-fraction multiplication expressions are represented by equal-size pieces in diagrams and by equal groups.
How to reason: Read a product as equal groups; match its numerators and denominators to a partitioned unit.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up: Number Talk: Three, Six, Nine, Twelve (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

Activity 1: Card Sort: Expressions and Diagrams (25 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(7 \times \frac{1}{8}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 2: Different Representations (10 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(6 \times \frac{1}{3}\), \(\frac{7}{2}\), \(4 \times \frac{1}{3}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.
Original source Cool-down is access-restricted/unverified; Edulytics substitutes goal-aligned independently authored teacher-reviewed exit prompt.
Edulytics worked model: How much do 7 groups of 1/8 represent?. Explain every transformation and check using equal wholes/units.
Open reflection: Source card sort includes original blackline diagrams; matching and drawing are teacher led.

KeyConcepts.Title: Match a picture to a multiplication expression

KeyConcepts.Rule: A drawing of n groups of 1/d matches n×(1/d) and gives n/d.

WorkedExamples.Title: Edulytics representation: three sixths
WorkedExamples.Question: A model shows three groups each containing 1/6 of an identical whole. Write the total.
WorkedExamples.Method: Translate equal groups into multiplication, then simplify.
Steps: Identify three equally sized groups each worth 1/6.
Simplify 3/6 by dividing numerator and denominator by 3.
WorkedExamples.Check: Teacher reviews the student's independently drawn diagram.

WorkedExamples.Title: Edulytics representation: five quarters
WorkedExamples.Question: Five groups each contain 1/4 of a whole. Write the total as a mixed number.
WorkedExamples.Method: Multiply groups by unit size, then divide the numerator by the denominator.
Steps: Five groups of one quarter mean 5×1/4.
Count five quarter pieces to obtain 5/4.
Regroup four quarters as 1 whole, with one quarter left.
WorkedExamples.Check: Preserve the same-sized whole in every group.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Counting drawn partitions without checking that all wholes have equal size.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It does not preserve the intended mathematical relationship or original task condition.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Read a product as equal groups; match its numerators and denominators to a partitioned unit.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Counting three groups of sixths as 3/3.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The whole remains partitioned into six equal parts.
